text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- International human rights group Amnesty International repeats appeal to President Sali Berisha to free Socialist opposition leader Fatos Nano.

- Disgruntled investors file suit against former bricklayer-turned-trader Aleksander Grunasi who has disappeared without accounting for 13 million dollars he collected from investment schemes promising high returns.
- President Sali Berisha vows to stem the flow of Albanians clandestinely travelling by sea to Italy.

- Azem Hajdari, a ruling Democratic Party member who has named himself leader of the Independent Trade Unions, has asked the International Monetary Fund to take control of the country's "get-rich-quick" pyramid schemes until Albania can establish a competitive banking system.
- Hajadri has sued the current leader of the Independent Trade Unions Valer Xheka on allegations he pocketed foreign aid and property from the union.
- The Albanian government has approved sending an Albanian peacekeeping mission to Zaire.
- President Berisha and the leader of ethnic Albanians in Serbia's Kosovo province said the opening of a representative office in the regional capital Prishtina would be tantamount to stability.
